name: Tomoya Iwata
about:
Tomoya Iwata is a curator and has directed The 5th Floor since April 2022. The 5th Floor is a curatorial space on the fifth floor of a former dormitory building in Ikenohata, a few minutes from Nezu station in Taito-ku. Since opening in 2020 it has centred on curation itself, with around 40 exhibitions by some 50 curators in its first four years and a curator-in-residence programme.

In autumn 2026 Iwata curated 'Portal: AfroAsia' (16 Oct - 29 Nov 2026) with AfroAsia Collective (Che Onejoon and Sun A Moon). In 2025 the space hosted 'Phenomena and Records: One Record, Three Rooms' (Aug - Oct 2025).

For a visiting artist or curator, he is a good contact for small, research-led exhibition projects and curatorial exchange in Tokyo. This is a non-commercial context, not a sales gallery.
notes: Role quote on the5thfloor.org curator bio: '2022年4月より、キュラトリアル・スペースThe 5th Floorのディレクターを務める'. Supporting pages: Forbes Japan 2024-02-20 (40 shows, 50 curators, curator residency) https://forbesjapan.com/articles/detail/69235 ; TAB 2025 show listing https://www.tokyoartbeat.com/events/-/Phenomena-and-Records-One-Record-Three-Rooms/5-C2-E814-D/2025-08-29. role_label: he is 'director' of the space, mapped to Artistic director.

name: Mai Endo
about:
Mai Endo is a Tokyo-based artist and actor. In 2018 she co-founded Multiple Spirits with the curator Mika Maruyama. It is a bilingual Japanese-English zine and research platform on queer feminist art practice, and through it Endo also curates and organises.

Art Week Tokyo 2026 (4-8 Nov) invited Multiple Spirits as one of the ten AWT Focus curators. The collective presents 'Patchwork of Ruffled Wings' at Waitingroom, with printed matter, textiles and works by Japanese and international artists. Earlier work includes 'Anytime Lunatic - Family Abolition' at gallery αM (2024), Roppongi Crossing 2025 and Invocation #4: Tokyo (2025). Art Basel's 2026 Tokyo city film features her guiding viewers through the city's artist-run spaces.

For a visiting artist working on queer or feminist themes, she is a key contact in Tokyo's independent scene.
notes: Primarily an artist. Her curatorial role comes through the Multiple Spirits collective, which AWT credits as curator. Score 3 per brief (AWT experimental side); the collective itself is grassroots. Co-founder Mika Maruyama not added: a search result says she is based in Vienna; not verified on an opened page. Other pages: https://www.artweektokyo.com/en/focus-en/ ; https://www.artbasel.com/stories/art-week-tokyo-2026-city-stories ; name_ja from https://bijutsutecho.com/artists/1285. Venue Waitingroom is a commercial gallery; she is listed for the collective, not the venue.
